title: "The biggest challenge in your stack? Evals, Evals, Evals" - 2026 State of AI Engineering results
talk_summary: A 1,048-respondent survey of AI engineers reports evals as the top stack challenge, cost as a first-class constraint, and widespread multi-model routing. Agents increasingly have write access but controls remain mostly human approvals and permission gating, while cheap generation raises review burden and context loss is a top failure mode.

takeaways.what_they_do: Teams monitor cost and token usage alongside quality, and cost regularly changes how ambitiously they use AI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: cost and token usage as the number two thing they watch for. It's being monitored like an SLA right under quality itself.
takeaways.numbers: 40% say cost regularly shapes ambition; 36% sometimes; cost/token usage is #2 monitored item

takeaways.technique: Task-type and cost routing plus multi-model comparison
takeaways.what_they_do: Most teams use more than one model; common mechanisms are routing by task type, comparing outputs from multiple models, and routing by cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Most popular is routing by task type. Some run multiple models compare outputs. Some route based on cost.
takeaways.numbers: 87% use more than one model; 94% use closed models; 45% use open-weight models; >90% of open-weight users also use closed

takeaways.technique: Small golden-set evals instead of vibe review
takeaways.what_they_do: Evals are the top stack challenge, yet the most common evaluation method remains vibe review; teams have not standardized eval methods.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the leading challenge, how to evaluate your AI outputs requires many different methods, but as always, the vibe review is number one.
takeaways.numbers: Evals are #1 challenge by a thin margin; 96% report some stack problem

takeaways.technique: Plan review capacity for cheap generation
takeaways.what_they_do: Cheap code generation increases experimentation but also increases review burden, so teams need review capacity and triage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the same tool that increases experimentation also increases review burden. Both can be true.
takeaways.numbers: Over 9 in 10 report negative downstream effects; 59% fear long-term liabilities

takeaways.what_they_do: The most common agent controls are human-in-the-loop approvals and gating permissions, even as more agents get write access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The top two are human in the loop approvals and gating permissions which are the right instincts
takeaways.numbers: 95% use agents; 89% of agent teams have write access; write-enabled share tripled vs last year

takeaways.what_they_do: Respondents report agent failures are more about thinking than plumbing, with hallucination or losing context mid-task as the top frustration; persistent memory/context is an active area.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hallucination or losing context mid task is what frustrates them the most.
takeaways.numbers: About two-thirds cite hallucination or losing context mid-task as most frustrating
